text: On the basis of the information received, the Commission shall establish, publish and maintain a list of certified qualified electronic signature creation devices.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, define formats and procedures applicable for the purpose of paragraph 1. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The process for the validation of a qualified electronic signature shall confirm the validity of a qualified electronic signature provided that:
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: a
text: the certificate that supports the signature was, at the time of signing, a qualified certificate for electronic signature complying with Annex I;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: b
text: the qualified certificate was issued by a qualified trust service provider and was valid at the time of signing;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: c
text: the signature validation data corresponds to the data provided to the relying party;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: d
text: the unique set of data representing the signatory in the certificate is correctly provided to the relying party;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: e
text: the use of any pseudonym is clearly indicated to the relying party if a pseudonym was used at the time of signing;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: f
text: the electronic signature was created by a qualified electronic signature creation device;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: g
text: the integrity of the signed data has not been compromised;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: h
text: the requirements provided for in Article 26 were met at the time of signing.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The system used for validating the qualified electronic signature shall provide to the relying party the correct result of the validation process and shall allow the relying party to detect any security relevant issues.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, establish reference numbers of standards for the validation of qualified electronic signatures. Compliance with the requirements laid down in paragraph 1 shall be presumed where the validation of qualified electronic signatures meets those standards. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: A qualified validation service for qualified electronic signatures may only be provided by a qualified trust service provider who:
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: a
text: provides validation in compliance with Article 32(1); and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: b
text: allows relying parties to receive the result of the validation process in an automated manner, which is reliable, efficient and bears the advanced electronic signature or advanced electronic seal of the provider of the qualified validation service.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, establish reference numbers of standards for qualified validation service referred to in paragraph 1. Compliance with the requirements laid down in paragraph 1 shall be presumed where the validation service for a qualified electronic signature meets those standards. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: A qualified preservation service for qualified electronic signatures may only be provided by a qualified trust service provider that uses procedures and technologies capable of extending the trustworthiness of the qualified electronic signature beyond the technological validity period.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, establish reference numbers of standards for the qualified preservation service for qualified electronic signatures. Compliance with the requirements laid down in paragraph 1 shall be presumed where the arrangements for the qualified preservation service for qualified electronic signatures meet those standards. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: An electronic seal shall not be denied legal effect and admissibility as evidence in legal proceedings solely on the grounds that it is in an electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements for qualified electronic seals.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: A qualified electronic seal shall enjoy the presumption of integrity of the data and of correctness of the origin of that data to which the qualified electronic seal is linked.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: A qualified electronic seal based on a qualified certificate issued in one Member State shall be recognised as a qualified electronic seal in all other Member States.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: An advanced electronic seal shall meet the following requirements:
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: a
text: it is uniquely linked to the creator of the seal;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: b
text: it is capable of identifying the creator of the seal;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: c
text: it is created using electronic seal creation data that the creator of the seal can, with a high level of confidence under its control, use for electronic seal creation; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: d
text: it is linked to the data to which it relates in such a way that any subsequent change in the data is detectable.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: If a Member State requires an advanced electronic seal in order to use an online service offered by, or on behalf of, a public sector body, that Member State shall recognise advanced electronic seals, advanced electronic seals based on a qualified certificate for electronic seals and qualified electronic seals at least in the formats or using methods defined in the implementing acts referred to in paragraph 5.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: If a Member State requires an advanced electronic seal based on a qualified certificate in order to use an online service offered by, or on behalf of, a public sector body, that Member State shall recognise advanced electronic seals based on a qualified certificate and qualified electronic seal at least in the formats or using methods defined in the implementing acts referred to in paragraph 5.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Member States shall not request for the cross-border use in an online service offered by a public sector body an electronic seal at a higher security level than the qualified electronic seal.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, establish reference numbers of standards for advanced electronic seals. Compliance with the requirements for advanced electronic seals referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article and Article 36 shall be presumed when an advanced electronic seal meets those standards. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: By 18 September 2015, and taking into account existing practices, standards and legal acts of the Union, the Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, define reference formats of advanced electronic seals or reference methods where alternative formats are used. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Qualified certificates for electronic seals shall meet the requirements laid down in Annex III.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Qualified certificates for electronic seals shall not be subject to any mandatory requirements exceeding the requirements laid down in Annex III.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Qualified certificates for electronic seals may include non-mandatory additional specific attributes. Those attributes shall not affect the interoperability and recognition of qualified electronic seals.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: If a qualified certificate for an electronic seal has been revoked after initial activation, it shall lose its validity from the moment of its revocation, and its status shall not in any circumstances be reverted.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Subject to the following conditions, Member States may lay down national rules on temporary suspension of qualified certificates for electronic seals:
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: a
text: if a qualified certificate for electronic seal has been temporarily suspended, that certificate shall lose its validity for the period of suspension;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: b
text: the period of suspension shall be clearly indicated in the certificate database and the suspension status shall be visible, during the period of suspension, from the service providing information on the status of the certificate.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, establish reference numbers of standards for qualified certificates for electronic seals. Compliance with the requirements laid down in Annex III shall be presumed where a qualified certificate for electronic seal meets those standards. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Article 29 shall apply mutatis mutandis to requirements for qualified electronic seal creation devices.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Article 30 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the certification of qualified electronic seal creation devices.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Article 31 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the publication of a list of certified qualified electronic seal creation devices.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Articles 32, 33 and 34 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the validation and preservation of qualified electronic seals.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: An electronic time stamp shall not be denied legal effect and admissibility as evidence in legal proceedings solely on the grounds that it is in an electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements of the qualified electronic time stamp.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: A qualified electronic time stamp shall enjoy the presumption of the accuracy of the date and the time it indicates and the integrity of the data to which the date and time are bound.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: A qualified electronic time stamp issued in one Member State shall be recognised as a qualified electronic time stamp in all Member States.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: A qualified electronic time stamp shall meet the following requirements:
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: a
text: it binds the date and time to data in such a manner as to reasonably preclude the possibility of the data being changed undetectably;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: b
text: it is based on an accurate time source linked to Coordinated Universal Time; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: c
text: it is signed using an advanced electronic signature or sealed with an advanced electronic seal of the qualified trust service provider, or by some equivalent method.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, establish reference numbers of standards for the binding of date and time to data and for accurate time sources. Compliance with the requirements laid down in paragraph 1 shall be presumed where the binding of date and time to data and the accurate time source meets those standards. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Data sent and received using an electronic registered delivery service shall not be denied legal effect and admissibility as evidence in legal proceedings solely on the grounds that it is in an electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements of the qualified electronic registered delivery service.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Data sent and received using a qualified electronic registered delivery service shall enjoy the presumption of the integrity of the data, the sending of that data by the identified sender, its receipt by the identified addressee and the accuracy of the date and time of sending and receipt indicated by the qualified electronic registered delivery service.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Qualified electronic registered delivery services shall meet the following requirements:
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: a
text: they are provided by one or more qualified trust service provider(s);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: b
text: they ensure with a high level of confidence the identification of the sender;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: c
text: they ensure the identification of the addressee before the delivery of the data;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: d
text: the sending and receiving of data is secured by an advanced electronic signature or an advanced electronic seal of a qualified trust service provider in such a manner as to preclude the possibility of the data being changed undetectably;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: e
text: any change of the data needed for the purpose of sending or receiving the data is clearly indicated to the sender and addressee of the data;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: f
text: the date and time of sending, receiving and any change of data are indicated by a qualified electronic time stamp.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: In the event of the data being transferred between two or more qualified trust service providers, the requirements in points (a) to (f) shall apply to all the qualified trust service providers.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, establish reference numbers of standards for processes for sending and receiving data. Compliance with the requirements laid down in paragraph 1 shall be presumed where the process for sending and receiving data meets those standards. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Qualified certificates for website authentication shall meet the requirements laid down in Annex IV.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, establish reference numbers of standards for qualified certificates for website authentication. Compliance with the requirements laid down in Annex IV shall be presumed where a qualified certificate for website authentication meets those standards. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: An electronic document shall not be denied legal effect and admissibility as evidence in legal proceedings solely on the grounds that it is in electronic form.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 30(4) shall be conferred on the Commission for an indeterminate period of time from 17 September 2014.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The delegation of power referred to in Article 30(4) may be revoked at any time by the European Parliament or by the Council. A decision to revoke shall put an end to the delegation of the power specified in that decision. It shall take specified therein. It shall not affect the validity of any delegated acts already in force.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: As soon as it adopts a delegated act, the Commission shall notify it simultaneously to the European Parliament and to the Council.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: A delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 30(4) shall enter into force only if no objection has been expressed either by the European Parliament or the Council within a period of two months of notification of that act to the European Parliament and the Council or if, before the expiry of that period, the European Parliament and the Council have both informed the Commission that they will not object. That period shall be extended by two months at the initiative of the European Parliament or of the Council.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The Commission shall be assisted by a committee. That committee shall be a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Where reference is made to this paragraph, Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 shall apply.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The Commission shall review the application of this Regulation and shall report to the European Parliament and to the Council no later than 1 July 2020. The Commission shall evaluate in particular whether it is appropriate to modify the scope of this Regulation or its specific provisions, including Article 6, point (f) of Article 7 and Articles 34, 43, 44 and 45, taking into account the experience gained in the application of this Regulation, as well as technological, market and legal developments.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: The report referred to in the first paragraph shall be accompanied, where appropriate, by legislative proposals.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: In addition, the Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and the Council every four years after the report referred to in the first paragraph on the progress towards achieving the objectives of this Regulation.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Directive 1999/93/EC is repealed with effect from 1 July 2016.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: References to the repealed Directive shall be construed as references to this Regulation.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Secure signature creation devices of which the conformity has been determined in accordance with Article 3(4) of Directive 1999/93/EC shall be considered as qualified electronic signature creation devices under this Regulation.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Qualified certificates issued to natural persons under Directive 1999/93/EC shall be considered as qualified certificates for electronic signatures under this Regulation until they expire.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: A certification-service-provider issuing qualified certificates under Directive 1999/93/EC shall submit a conformity assessment report to the supervisory body as soon as possible but not later than 1 July 2017. Until the submission of such a conformity assessment report and the completion of its assessment by the supervisory body, that certification- service-provider shall be considered as qualified trust service provider under this Regulation.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: If a certification-service-provider issuing qualified certificates under Directive 1999/93/EC does not submit a conformity assessment report to the supervisory body within the time limit referred to in paragraph 3, that certification-service-provider shall not be considered as qualified trust service provider under this Regulation from 2 July 2017.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: This Regulation shall apply from 1 July 2016, except for the following:
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: a
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: b
text: Article 7, Article 8(1) and (2), Articles 9, 10, 11 and Article 12(1) shall apply from the date of application of the implementing acts referred to in Articles 8(3) and 12(8);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

label: c
text: Article 6 shall apply from three years as from the date of application of the implementing acts referred to in Articles 8(3) and 12(8).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Where the notified electronic identification scheme is included in the list published by the Commission pursuant to Article 9 before the date referred to in point (c) of paragraph 2 of this Article, the recognition of the electronic identification means under that scheme pursuant to Article 6 shall take place no later than 12 months after the publication of that scheme but not before the date referred to in point (c) of paragraph 2 of this Article.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Notwithstanding point (c) of paragraph 2 of this Article, a Member State may decide that electronic identification means under electronic identification scheme notified pursuant to Article 9(1) by another Member State are recognised in the first Member State as from the date of application of the implementing acts referred to in Articles 8(3) and 12(8). Member States concerned shall inform the Commission. The Commission shall make this information public.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: Done at Brussels, 23 July 2014.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/eIDAS Regulation (Electronic Identification and Trust Services).pdf

text: For the Parliament For the Council The President The President M. SCHULZ S. GOZI
